diffuseAlbedo.note: Golden olive-brown, silky (the 金丝 chatoyance is not modelled); no measured colour was read: a first value read from trade and museum photographs of the named material.

refractiveIndex.source: Marschner, S.R., Westin, S.H., Arbree, A. & Moon, J.T. (2005) Measuring and modeling the appearance of finished wood, ACM Transactions on Graphics 24(3) (as cited in the timber records)

porosity.derivation: 1 - 480 / 1500: the density over the cell wall's own (about 1500 kg/m3, Siau 1995, as the oak's)

wettingDepth.note: As the oak: the depth a finish soaks into.

grain.source: Wu, J., Liang, J., Chen, M., Zheng, S. & Xu, J. (2022) Study on the structural characteristics and physical and mechanical properties of Phoebe bournei thinning wood. Journal of Renewable Materials 10(11), https://www.techscience.com/jrm/v10n11/48716/html
grain.note: Confirmed. Mean tangential vessel diameter 72 um, maximum 111 um, about 19 vessels per mm2 (vessel proportion 12.89 %). The trees are P. bournei, 14-year-old plantation thinnings. This record is named P. zhennan, but its research record covers both species and uses this paper for density.

bed.source: Wu, J., Liang, J., Chen, M., Zheng, S. & Xu, J. (2022) Study on the structural characteristics and physical and mechanical properties of Phoebe bournei thinning wood. Journal of Renewable Materials 10(11), https://www.techscience.com/jrm/v10n11/48716/html
bed.note: Confirmed: growth-ring width averages 4.99 mm and decreases gradually from pith to bark. These are young plantation stems, so boards from older trees would have narrower rings. That matches the museum's stated plantation-grown phoebe.

bedAspect.note: How much coarser the figure is along the grain than across it.

hurst.source: Candela et al. 2012, Journal of Geophysical Research 117, B08409 (fault surfaces, 0.6 to 0.8; cited in Stone.ush)
hurst.note: The middle of the range measured on rock surfaces, as the travertine's.

toneSpread.note: A first half-range of ln(albedo) across one face.

roughnessSpread.note: A first half-range of ln(roughness), as the oak's.

rayFleck.source: Wu, J., Liang, J., Chen, M., Zheng, S. & Xu, J. (2022) Study on the structural characteristics and physical and mechanical properties of Phoebe bournei thinning wood. Journal of Renewable Materials 10(11), https://www.techscience.com/jrm/v10n11/48716/html (ray tissue proportion 10.24 %)
rayFleck.note: Confirmed 10.24 % rays (fibres 64.83 %, axial parenchyma 11.23 %). The figure counts uniseriate and multiseriate rays together. Multiseriate rays are only about 22 um wide, so they read as fine silk, not oak-like fleck, and rayTone should stay near 1.
rayFleck.derivation: Delesse's principle: for a section plane of any fixed orientation placed at random, the expected area share of a phase equals its volume share. The ray share of a quarter-sawn face is therefore about the ray volume proportion, 0.1024.

rayLength.source: Wu, J., Liang, J., Chen, M., Zheng, S. & Xu, J. (2022) Study on the structural characteristics and physical and mechanical properties of Phoebe bournei thinning wood. Journal of Renewable Materials 10(11), https://www.techscience.com/jrm/v10n11/48716/html
rayLength.note: Confirmed. Multiseriate ray height is 81-726 um, mean 275 um (5-30 cells). Uniseriate rays are 54-179 um, mean 104 um (2-5 cells). MatterWood.h / Wood.ush define rayLength as 'a fleck's length along the grain'. On a quarter-sawn (radial) face that is the ray's axial height, so this is the right quantity.
